articles.title: Carlisle Launches EL121 Disc Brakes for Improved Performance and Wear Life

paras.en: Carlisle Launches EL121 Disc Brakes for Improved Performance and Wear Life

(MEDINA, OH, September 12, 2023) – Carlisle Brake & Friction is excited to announce the launch of EL121 Disc Brake Pads for mine haul truck applications. The new product series will be named Extended Life, or the EL Series, and EL121 will be the first friction formulation of the series to launch.

Carlisle’s EL121 Series friction material nearly doubles the service life of front-axle, mine haul truck brake pads. The result is increased equipment uptime, and reduced maintenance costs when utilizing the OEM calipers and rotors.

Autonomous haul trucks experience higher pad temperatures, which drive elevated pad wear from increased braking cycles as the retarder and the service brake are applied. EL121 features a highly wear-resistant friction material blend that provides extended brake pad life with consistent and fade-resistant braking performance. EL121 is the ideal solution for today’s autonomous mine haul trucks (may also be used in manned mine haul trucks for increased performance and longevity).

“We understand that mine operators need to keep their haul trucks on the job and not in the shop for brake service. Our latest innovation allows for up to double the service life of the front-axle mine haul truck brake pads and are a will-fit replacement to existing OEM pads. These were thoroughly lab tested as well as field tested on Komatsu 830E-1 trucks,” said Ron Ratell, Product Line Director Friction Products at Carlisle Brake & Friction.

EL121 friction has been dyno tested to replicate the application and is proven to deliver an innovative, high-energy material to meet market needs. EL121 disc brake pads also feature an industry-proven mechanical retention system with backing plate technology designed for superior bonding and durability, capable of withstanding abusive conditions in even the harshest Off-Highway environments.

Carlisle’s EL121 Series disc brake pads are available now through authorized Carlisle dealers and distributors. To learn more, visit https://www.carlislecbf.com/products/brake-friction/disc-brake-pads/off-highway-disc-brake-pads/el. To locate an authorized Carlisle dealer near you, search our online distributor listing https://www.carlislecbf.com/support/find-a-distributor.

Carlisle Brake & Friction is a globally recognized leader in the development and manufacture of highly innovative brake and friction system solutions to service a diverse range of motion control applications. The comprehensive nature of Carlisle’s brake system expertise includes hydraulic control products, industrial brake assemblies, wet and dry friction material for brake, clutch, and transmission applications as well as aftermarket replacement products. Our full-system product offering, supported by our industry-experience staff of experts, provides our customers with brake system solutions that set them apart from their competition. www.carlislecbf.com

articles.title: Carlisle Suzhou Achieves Caterpillar SER Certification

paras.en: Carlisle Suzhou Achieves Caterpillar SER Certification

(MEDINA, January 25, 2024) – Carlisle Brake & Friction announced its Suzhou facility has won a Supplier Excellence Recognition (SER) Certification from Caterpillar Inc. The Caterpillar SER is a new supplier management system featuring "Certified" and "Excellent" levels. Caterpillar officially launched the program in 2022. Carlisle's Suzhou manufacturing facility achieved a "Certified" level of recognition and celebrated the achievement alongside the Caterpillar team with a ceremony at the Carlisle Suzhou plant.

articles.title: SEMA Crowns Champion of Bike Builder Shootout
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: The inaugural SEMA Battle of the Builders: Bike Builder Shootout presented by Mothers named Steven Iacona as its first champion. Iacona won with a custom Harley-Davidson Knucklehead, rising to the top of a competitive field of builders from across the country.

“It’s amazing. I’ve never been to the SEMA Show before, but it’s always been something I’ve wanted to experience,” said Iacona, owner of Iacona Custom Cycles in Brooklyn, N.Y. “To be next to these great builders on stage, it’s just incredible. It’s a great thing for the motorcycle industry, and it’s great to bring new life into the industry.”

The competition was evaluated by a panel of motorcycle industry experts, including Zach Ness of Arlen Ness Motorcycles, Jeff Holt of V-Twin Visionary and Pat Patterson of Led Sled Customs. Judges reviewed entries based on craftsmanship, design innovation and overall execution before selecting finalists and naming Iacona the overall champion.

“I began with a 1945 Knucklehead engine that we had, and I just needed to find the right customer that would let me do what I wanted with it,” said Iacona. “I built a bike similar to what I had heard the stock Knucklehead was and just enhanced it. I didn’t want to disrespect the Knucklehead, and this is what I came up with. The customer is going to ride it and enjoy it, and that’s all that matters.”
- Winner: Steven Iacona — Harley-Davidson Knucklehead
- 2nd place: Robert Zeolla — Indian In-Line 4
- 3rd place: James Crosby — Harley-Davidson Pan Head

The addition of the motorcycle category reflects SEMA’s commitment to expanding opportunities across the specialty-equipment industry and strengthening the powersports presence at the SEMA Show. The competition recognizes builders who push innovation, craftsmanship and creativity within motorcycle customization.

“The Bike Builder Shootout reflects SEMA’s support for every segment of the customization industry and creating new opportunities for builders to showcase their work,” said RJ de Vera, vice president of marketing for SEMA. “The creativity and craftsmanship displayed throughout this competition exceeded our expectations. We’re excited to build on this momentum and further expand the powersports presence at the SEMA Show in the years ahead.”

The Bike Builder Shootout was introduced in 2026 as an expansion of the SEMA Battle of the Builders competition, creating a dedicated platform for motorcycle builders to showcase their work on a major industry stage. The category celebrates the artistry, engineering, and passion driving motorcycle customization.
For more information about SEMA Battle of the Builders, visit semabotb.com.

articles.title: Mitchell 1’s ProDemand+ Connects Mechanical and Collision Repair Data
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: Mitchell 1 introduces ProDemand+, integrating OEM collision repair information within its ProDemand platform. By connecting collision and mechanical repair resources, ProDemand+ helps auto body shops streamline research, identify related repair requirements and tackle more complex repairs involving interconnected vehicle systems.

“Collision repairs today involve much more than fixing visible damage. Even a seemingly straightforward bumper or mirror replacement can involve electrical systems, sensors and critical calibration procedures,” said Chris Bonneau, product marketing manager for collision products for Mitchell 1. “ProDemand+ gives technicians access to the OEM information they need to identify related mechanical repair requirements upfront, reduce costly rework and get vehicles safely back on the road faster.”

For example, replacing a damaged bumper may require technicians to research electrical connections, mounting specifications and ADAS sensor locations and calibration procedures. With ProDemand+, collision professionals can access this information alongside OEM body repair procedures without switching between separate repair information platforms.

ProDemand+ combines OEM body and structural repair procedures, sectioning information, materials, adhesives, and paint and refinishing resources with ProDemand’s mechanical repair information. To help technicians research related vehicle systems, the platform also provides vehicle-specific ADAS procedures, interactive wiring diagrams for electrical troubleshooting, SureTrack Real Fixes and community forums featuring proven repair solutions and insights from professional technicians.
For more information, visit mitchell1.com, call (888) 724-6742 or locate an independent sales consultant at mitchell1.com/my-rep.

articles.title: BendPak Debuts Valor C10 Custom 1970 Chevy Pickup at SEMA
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: BendPak Inc. unveiled its inaugural custom-built vehicle at the 2026 SEMA Show last week. The Valor C10 is a handcrafted 1970 Chevrolet C10 pickup truck built as a tribute to the sacrifice, courage and commitment of the U.S. Armed Forces.

“We call this build the Valor C10 — it was created to honor the brave men and women who have served and continue to serve in our armed forces, especially those who gave their lives in defense of our nation,” said Jeff Kritzer, president and CEO of BendPak. “BendPak proudly supports the military community. This serves as our way of saying thank you and reminding everyone that freedom isn’t free.”

As the nation observes Veterans Day, the Valor C10 carries personal meaning for BendPak’s leadership and team. U.S. Army veteran Don Henthorn founded BendPak in 1965. After three years of active-duty service as a U.S. Air Force C-130 loadmaster, Kritzer transitioned to the Air National Guard, retaining his flight status and loadmaster duties while launching his full-time career at BendPak, a dual commitment he maintained for three years. He is the son of a senior master sergeant and fellow loadmaster whose life was devoted to military service. Kritzer’s son, Devin, served in the U.S. Army, including deployments to the Gulf region and Bangladesh.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: With its fusion of modern performance and timeless design, the Valor C10 emphasizes American strength, ingenuity and resilience.
The team at Nostalgia Hot Rods, led by Dustin Hacker, was tapped to build the Valor C10.

“We’ve worked with Dustin for several years, supplying his shops with BendPak lifts and equipment, as well as showcasing many of his amazing builds in our SEMA Show booths,” said Sean Price, director of product development for BendPak. “We knew he had the passion and craftsmanship to bring our vision for the Valor C10 to life.”
Hacker started with a vintage C10, and by the time the build was complete, the closest part left to stock was a heavily modified cab.

“Most of the sheet metal is custom-fabricated, including the roof, hood, drip rails, floors, bumpers, engine bay and bed,” said Hacker. “Under the hood, there’s a 376-cubic-inch V8 with a 2.9-liter Whipple supercharger. This thing will make 750 horsepower and drive like a dream.”

Despite its slammed stance, the body-dropped C10 retains more than 4.5 inches of usable ground clearance due to the chassis setup, making it easier to navigate speed bumps and driveways. It’s finished in metallic blue with red accents, including a body stripe, brake calipers and engine. The color scheme nods to the U.S. flag. Custom Valor C10 badges designed by the BendPak creative team highlight both doors.
The interior features a classic bench seat upholstered in two-tone gray Alcantara with blue stitching. The door panels and headliner are also bespoke.
- BTR Gen V Stage 2 supercharged camshaft
- Holley Terminator X Max engine management system
- Gearstar GM 6L80E 6-speed automatic transmission
- Custom Eddie Motorsports serpentine system
- QA1 4-way adjustable coilovers with cantilever rear suspension
- PCS electronic gear shift module with wireless paddle shifter
- Dapper Lighting custom headlights and taillights with custom billet housings
Get all the specs, view the Valor C10 build process and watch its SEMA Show reveal at BendPak.com/valorc10.

articles.title: NHTSA estimates decline in traffic fatalities in first half of 2026
articles.author: Lurah Lowery

paras.en: Newly released data from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) estimates a 2.5% drop in traffic fatalities for the first half of 2026, projecting the second-lowest half-year fatality rate in U.S. history.
Crash fatalities fell to an estimated 16,750 from January through June, down from 17,175 during the first half of 2025.

“We’ve made progress on road safety, but the Trump Administration isn’t letting up,” said NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison in a NHTSA press release. “Even with near-record low fatality rates, we will continue to work with a sense of urgency to make sure more Americans get home safely. Through our Pathways to Safer Streets initiative, we are tackling the leading causes of traffic deaths— from reckless driving to impaired driving—while funding critical lifesaving measures like prehospital blood programs.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Vehicle miles traveled (VMT) increased about 12.9 billion miles, or 0.8%, in the first half of the year, while the fatality rate fell to a near-record low of 1.02 per 100 million VMT. If realized, the fatality rate would be the second-lowest first-half rate, slightly above the lowest reached in the first half of 2014 at 1.01.
In the first half of 2025, NHTSA estimated the fatality rate was 1.05 per 100 million VMT.
Fatalities in Q2 2026 decreased by 0.2%.
Thirty-five states and Puerto Rico are projected to have had fatality decreases during the first half of 2026.

NHTSA notes in its report that the fatality counts and percentage change for 2025 and 2026 will be slightly revised when the Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS) Annual Reporting File (ARF) for 2025 is available later this year, and when the final file for 2025 and the ARF for 2026 are available next year. Estimates will be further refined when projections for January through September of 2026 are released in late December.
Historically, the report points out that fatalities increased for seven consecutive quarters beginning in Q3 2020 until a 5.9% decline in Q2 2022.
The percentage increase in the second quarter of 2021 is the highest quarterly percentage increase in FARS data recorded history, which was in the COVID-19 pandemic period, according to the report.
Eight out of 10 regions broken out in NHTSA’s data saw fewer fatalities during the first half of this year compared to the first half of 2025.
In 2026, Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy directed NHTSA to launch the Pathways to Safer Streets (P2SS) action plan.

Under the P2SS framework, NHTSA says it is partnering with law enforcement agencies nationwide “to support vigorous, high-visibility traffic enforcement aimed at identifying and stopping dangerous drivers.”

“NHTSA has also increased support for prehospital blood transfusion programs for safety partners, enabling emergency medical services units to administer blood before crash victims reach the hospital,” the NHTSA press release states. “Research shows this innovation decreases mortality for trauma patients with severe bleeding by 37%.”

articles.title: Boyd to investors on Q3 total losses, TCOR, and repairable claims volumes
articles.author: Lurah Lowery

paras.en: Boyd Group President and CEO Brian Kaner said Wednesday that there is positive momentum in the industry to push total losses down.

Kaner made the comment during the company’s Q3 earnings call with investors. When asked how raising total loss thresholds impacts total loss rates, Kaner said he thinks rates could decrease with more regulation.
“If you see people raising thresholds to 85%, those borderline total losses will end up becoming repairable vehicles again and ultimately help our business,” he said.

“Total losses are getting a tremendous amount of attention in the industry right now. We know that it’s not a great customer experience. There’s more people that are upside down in loans right now, so if their car gets totaled, they end up not only not being able to get a car, but they end up writing a check to get out of the car that they’re actually in. We know that it’s not a great experience. I think many people are picking up on that, inclusive of the insurance carriers.”
He added that attrition after total losses is higher than after repairable claims, which has gotten the attention of insurance carriers and OEMs.

“If you trust the data that’s out there, the data that CCC would reflect or that JD Power reflects, is 40% of people after a total loss event switch insurance carriers, so the attrition after a total loss event versus a repair event that’s 7% is super high,” Kaner said.
He said Q3 claims data continues to point to a more stable operating environment, with repairable claims volumes estimated to be down 1–3% year over year.
Kaner also shared that Boyd saw a sequential improvement in total cost of repair (TCOR) in Q3.

“We said for quite some time that the underlying metrics behind TCOR were still moving as they normally move,” he said. “We still saw normal pricing increases on the labor side. We still saw normal price movement on parts through the inflationary environment that we’re in. And what had been muting that was just the year-over-year impact of more total losses, so bigger tickets coming out of the repair set driving down or mixing down the overall TCOR. We saw that level out in Q3, and we continue to see it now stable as we get into the fourth quarter. That’s allowing the underlying movement and price to actually illuminate.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Part of what’s driving TCOR up, Kaner said, is an increase in calibration services.

“We continue to see a higher penetration rate of calibration services on the average ticket that we’re seeing, and all of those things are starting to move the ticket back in a more positive direction,” he said. “I would say still muted from the, call it 4%, that we expect, but certainly moving its way back towards then.”

A press release on Q3 earnings results adds that “volume gains driven by the strength of the company’s performance and insurer relationships contributed to positive same-store sales growth during the quarter of 2.2%, complemented by a modest increase in total cost of repair.”
Kaner told investors that self-pay jobs are growing at a greater pace than insurance volume, though it’s growing off a much smaller base. He said the average self-pay ticket is much lower.
“Our focus today still remains on providing great service for the insurance partners that we do business with,” he said.
Regarding general Q3 earnings, Boyd reported a 28% revenue increase supported by the addition of Joe Hudson’s.
Kaner said the focus with integrating Joe Hudson’s is now on improving client scores to drive incremental volume and ensuring stores have adequate staffing.
Kaner also told investors that Boyd has 34 new startup locations planned for the next 12 months.

articles.title: NHTSA’s White to collision repairers: ‘You are the final checkpoint’
articles.author: Teresa Moss

paras.en: The collision repair industry has a bigger role in the national vehicle conversation than the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has historically recognized, Lee White, NHTSA’s deputy administrator, said during the Society of Collision Repair Specialists’ (SCRS) OEM Summit held during the 2026 SEMA Show.

“I’m excited to be here speaking with skilled craftsmen and women who bring vehicles back to life after they’ve had an accident,” White said. “When done right, your work is often underappreciated, even though it is the product of hard-won expertise.”
NHTSA exists because there is risk every time someone drives on U.S. roadways, White said.
In the 1970s, about 70,000 Americans died a year on U.S. roadways, he said. That number was reduced to about 39,000 in 2024, and the estimate is below 37,000 in 2025.

“That is a lot of progress, particularly when you consider how many more cars and trucks are on the road, as well as the miles that we drive,” he said. “NHTSA cannot take all the credit for this improvement. Many players have contributed, from local governments to the major vehicle manufacturers. There is a lot of work still to be done.”
NHTSA Administrator Jonathon Morrison frequently tells his staff that the agency cannot operate in a vacuum, White said.

“We are opening up our doors to all our stakeholders and the experts like those in the room,” White said. “We want to team with you, and we want to work with your team, and we want to hear from you. The collaborative spirit is exactly why I am here today. By working together, we can save lives.”
The Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (FMVSS) conversation typically revolves around how a vehicle is designed, White said.

“But reality tells us a different story,” White said. “A vehicle may be on the road for 15 to 20 years, experiencing multiple collisions and undergoing numerous repairs over its useful life. From NHTSA’s perspective, we must think deeply about how to preserve the safety performance engineered into a vehicle throughout its entire lifespan, and certify that there’s no degradation.”
NHTSA research on automatic emergency braking, for example, shows the technology prevents crashes, he said.

“We accept that these systems create a measurable safety benefit,” White said. “Preserving that capability after a collision must become a core part of how we think about vehicle safety. If a system was producing a measurable reduction in crash risk before a crash, our expectation must be that it will continue to do so after the vehicle leaves your repair facility.”

White added that looking for a warning light on the dashboard is not enough to safely evaluate vehicle damage. He said shops must verify that safety systems are performing before returning the vehicle to customers.
The complexity will grow as the vehicle fleet transitions to autonomous vehicles, he said.
White pointed to a recent partnership between NHTSA and SAE to expedite the development of data-driven AV performance standards.

“As we move toward vehicles assuming more of the driving task, the integrity of a collision repair becomes even more consequential,” White said. “The collision repair industry must start preparing for this right now. If we are ultimately going to trust a vehicle to make safety-critical decisions, it is absolutely essential to know that its sensing and decision-making capabilities have been properly restored following a collision.”
NHTSA needs data to better navigate the future, he said. He added this provides an opportunity for the collision repair industry and NHTSA to collaborate.

“Your facilities see damaged vehicles every day,” White said. “You are sitting on a potentially valuable source of safety information that historically hasn’t been part of the research ecosystem. The information coming out of a repair process could help NHTSA and manufacturers significantly better understand how safety systems perform in the real world.”
NHTSA wants comments from the collision industry, White said.

This includes during a 90-day comment period that will follow an ADAS Workshop on Aftermarket Modifications and ADAS Performance event Dec. 10. The event will bring together OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers, engineering firms, academics, and SEMA to talk about the issues, White said.

“We believe that this event will be an important step toward solutions,” White said. “Reconciling the different interests of all those involved may be challenging, but all involved can certainly agree that keeping safety is paramount.”
Aaron Schulenburg, SCRS executive director, sat down with White during the OEM Summit. He noted that NHTSA organically found individuals on SCRS’ ADAS Governing Council to join the event.
White said NHTSA will read every comment submitted following the event.
“Submit your comments,” White added. “We want to hear from you.”
Schulenburg asked what repair information might help NHTSA in the future.

“How can we learn more about certain repair issues that this room is having in terms of what needs to get back to the OEMs and what we can do to improve the safety profile,” White said. “It’s a matter of turning data into real-world steps we can take to make our roads safer, to make the vehicles perform at a safer rate, and to make our drivers’ behavior better. That’s our goal.”
The collision industry faces pressure that can lead to repairs that don’t necessarily restore the systems, Schulenburg responded.

“I think that’s where the data question comes in: how do we use that to connect the dots to incentivize proper repairs to restore the safety rather than allowing that pressure, the cost mitigation to influence the industry to move in different directions?, he asked.
White said he hopes that conversation becomes a part of the Dec. 10 event.

“The people in this room, you care about doing repairs the right way,” White said. “We want our rules and regulations to encourage that. We can’t make choices because of financial pressure. Financial pressure, wherever it’s coming from — internal to your company or from industry, if it’s coming from insurance, wherever that pressure point’s coming, it can’t be at the expense of safety. We can never let a vehicle go out of our shops and be at risk safety-wise because we chose cost.”
The event should identify what research is missing and what steps should be taken in the next 12 months, he said.
“We’ve got to make sure that we’ve got the voice, we’ve got the comments, we’ve got the gaps identified, so that we know what we’ve got to do,” he said.
A question from the audience asked White how NHTSA tracks alternative parts.

“If you see something, say something,” White said. “Go to the NHTSA website. You can fill out a form and let us know that you have an issue with a part that you’re concerned about. Whether it’s a comment that we issue from a conference or a notice of proposed rulemaking, there’s people in NHTSA that look at that and take that seriously.”

NHTSA has been raising the performance bar in other ways recently, White said. This includes incorporating new ADAS evaluations, such as automatic emergency braking, into its New Car Assessment Program (NCAP).
Automakers and vehicle safety groups told Congress last year that NCAP had fallen behind other countries and wasn’t rating new safety technologies fast enough.

White said under Morrison, NHTSA is evaluating not only whether it has the equipment but if it also performs. He pointed to an AEB final rule that specifies vehicle and pedestrian avoidance performance benchmarks on vehicles by 2029.

“Administrator Morrison has made it clear that many of our past regulations were designed when no one envisioned modern safety technologies, meaning that the technology of the future is often tethered to the regulations of the past,” White said. “To address this, under the leadership of President Trump and Transportation Secretary Duffy, NHTSA is diligently working to update the FMVSS to account for these new designs, prioritizing safety requirements and the performance of those requirements over design specifications.”

paras.en: The repair industry must also evolve as performance expectations become more sophisticated, White said.

“The critical question must shift from ‘did we calibrate it?’ to ‘have we restored its performance?’ Manufacturers, regulators, and repairers all have a shared role in establishing confidence that these systems continue to deliver their intended safety benefit after a crash,” White said.
Schulenburg asked whether NHTSA had any guidance on how the collision industry can navigate pressure it faces in the claims environment. For example, pressure to use alternative parts.
“Our worry as an industry is that oftentimes that may produce an outcome that doesn’t preserve the safety that you’ve worked so hard to create in the standards,” Schulenburg said.
White responded, “You are under tremendous pressure to cut costs. That can’t come at the expense of safety. Safety always has to be foundational.”
Affordability is also part of that equation, he added. Technology advancement must consider the cost of repair, he said.
Recently, an OEM announced six new model types that will sell below $40,000, he said.

“The message of affordability is a loud one,” White said. “How do we do that? What we don’t want is a safety system that only performs like it’s on the showroom floor. We can’t do that at the repair shops. That’s not an acceptable business model. How do we strike that balance? There are still a lot of details to work out, but we don’t want to put in any safety risk in that process.”

Schulenburg responded, “I think when consumers have to assume parts of the cost of the repair that they otherwise expected to be covered by a claim, those are pieces of affordability that don’t always get addressed. You’re obviously engaging with the repair community and the manufacturer community. Do you also engage with the insurance community around these topics?”
White said NHTSA has ongoing communications with the insurance industry as well. It also tries to stay up to date on trends.
Deadly counterfeit airbags are an example of how a decision made during a repair can determine whether a safety system protects someone or actually injures them, White said.

“That’s the lesson that NHTSA has learned and what collision repairers need to hear is that the traceability, the authenticity, and the suitability of the safety-critical replacement components are paramount,” he said. “We understand the pressure from the insurance companies on repairs to seek out alternative parts, lower their costs. But there’s an equal reason of concern when dealing with alternative safety sensors, cameras, and radar units.”

NHTSA identified an 11th death caused by a counterfeit airbag part from China in September. The agency urges owners of used vehicles that have previously been in a crash with an airbag deployment since 2020 to have their vehicle inspected.
The agency banned the importation and sale of these DTN60DB inflators earlier this year; the first ban NHTSA issued in more than two decades.
White said the sellers of counterfeit parts have short-term business models.
“They pop up, they disappear,” he said. “They go out of business, and then six months later they surface. We shut that one down, and then two days later they open up another marketplace.”
These are trends buyers can look for when looking for a reputable parts seller, he said.
Schulenburg responded that authorized supply channels play an important role in protecting against counterfeit parts.
He asked whether there is a risk for other counterfeit parts such as cameras, sensors, and radars.

“That’s a global threat as far as knockoffs and noncompliant equipment,” White responded. “We’re going to have to constantly be sure that we’ve got the right standards, sure that their performance levels are validated.”
Every OEM has different technology developments, he said. He added that each has a different level of performance.

“A lidar advancement means maybe it’s six months ahead of the radar and it’s a little bit ahead of the camera,” White said. “How do we make sure that that system performs like it was designed, at that same year model with similar equipment and similar mileage?”
There have to be some procedures and processes in place to keep technology performing after a collision, he said.
He noted that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has published some guidelines.
“NHTSA hasn’t done that in terms of the technology,” White said. “We are going to go after the performance of the system.”
Federal law prohibits any motor vehicle repair business from knowingly making a device or design element of a vehicle inoperative, he said.

“While the concept of not rendering inoperative a federally required safety system is not new, a lot of the technology found in modern vehicles is,” White said. “When a vehicle safety system performance depends on cameras, radar, software, precise mounting tolerances, calibration, and interconnected systems, the responsibility of the repairer is more complex than ever before.”
“Rendering inoperative” is a term used by NHTSA that defines the degradation of a safety system to where it doesn’t perform as it should.

Schulenburg pointed out that the rendering inoperative discussion historically has been focused on safety systems such as airbags and seatbelts. He asked how this could change with the advancement of technical safety systems.
“What’s happening is we’re moving toward a situation where the vehicle is going to be able to operate itself,” White said.
He added that the discussion of rendering inoperable grows in the scenario.
Schulenburg asked whether the recent elections will change the way that NHTSA operates.

“I’ll go back to the 100 people that are going to be killed in crashes today,” White said. “They’re not worried about elections. They want the safety equipment to work. The NHTSA mission transcends the politics in Washington, D.C. I’ve never met a team of more committed people working every day on safety.”
Looking forward, White said training technicians for future technology is one of the most important pieces for the collision repair industry.
“That’s where the energy needs to be, so that we’re prepared, so that as the technology comes out in 2027, 2028, 2029, and these model years start rolling out, we’re ready,” White said.
Collision repairers touch vehicles at a unique, critical moment after something goes wrong and before vehicles go back on the road, White said.

“There are profound opportunities for the collision repair community to become a more meaningful partner in NHTSA’s safety mission,” he added. “If there’s one thing I want everyone in the collision repair business in this room to understand about your role in vehicle safety, it is this: you are the final checkpoint. The safety standards we write and the system automakers engineer rely entirely on your expertise to ensure endurance throughout that vehicle’s life.”

Aaron Schulenburg, SCRS executive director, and Lee White, NHTSA’s deputy administrator, discuss the collision repair industry during SCRS’ OEM Summit at the 2026 SEMA Show (Lurah Lowery/Repairer Driven News).

articles.title: Does A Stop-Start Engine Demand Better Oil?
articles.author: Greg Jones

paras.en: Stop-start technology is designed to improve fuel efficiency and reduce emissions, but it also alters how engines operate, especially regarding lubrication.

Each time the engine shuts off and restarts, engine oil must quickly reach critical components like the valvetrain, camshafts and upper engine areas. These repeated cycles can increase wear if the oil does not respond quickly enough.
That’s why choosing the right oil, particularly a high-quality full synthetic, plays an important role in protecting performance and supporting long-term engine life.

Stop-start systems increase the frequency of engine restarts during everyday driving, particularly in traffic. Each restart requires oil to reestablish a protective layer across key components quickly.

While no unique oil category is required, performance characteristics become more important. Oils that circulate efficiently and maintain protection under repeated cycling are better suited for these engines. Full-synthetic oils are designed to deliver that level of consistency, helping reduce the impact of frequent restarts and reducing stress on components that drive the start-stop systems.

Vehicle manufacturer recommendations should always guide oil selection. For added protection, full-synthetic motor oils are well-suited to stop-start conditions due to their ability to withstand repeated stress.
High-quality synthetic oils are engineered to circulate efficiently during startup, protect critical components under frequent cycling, and maintain stability under varying temperatures.
These properties help ensure consistent lubrication throughout drives that involve frequent stopping and starting.

Stop-start operation increases the frequency of engine transitions from off to on, introducing more frequent periods when components rely on immediate lubrication. The upper engine, including cams and valvetrain components, can be especially sensitive during these transitions. Without fast and effective oil coverage, these areas may experience increased friction over time.

Premium synthetic oils are formulated to address this by maintaining strong film strength and resisting breakdown, even under repeated cycling. Conventional oil can meet basic requirements, but it is generally less effective in managing the demands of frequent engine cycling.
Synthetic oils are more stable and adaptable across changing conditions. This allows them to maintain consistent viscosity and protection, even as the engine repeatedly cools and restarts.
In stop-start environments, where conditions change rapidly, this consistency provides a measurable advantage in maintaining protection.
However, frequent stop-and-go driving may be categorized as severe service due to possible added strain placed on engine systems and fluids.

Shops should follow manufacturer-recommended oil change intervals; and check customers’ oil life monitoring systems when available. These factors can affect how quickly oil degrades, Even with high-quality formulations, oil can degrade more or less quickly depending on driving habits and other factors.

articles.title: Concept Tire Helps VW Set EV Efficiency World Record
articles.author: Christian Hinton

paras.en: A Continental concept tire contributed to three world records set by Volkswagen‘s Mission Efficiency electric concept vehicle during a long-distance drive.

The vehicle consumed 7.51 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of electricity per 100 kilometers (approx. 60 miles), including charging losses, and 6.89 kWh excluding charging losses. RID – Rekord-Institut für Deutschland certified the record on Aug. 24.

The Mission Efficiency traveled 1,278.36 kilometers (approx. 790 miles) from Wolfsburg to Vienna under real-world conditions. The journey required one charging stop, and the vehicle finished with 164 kilometers (approx. 100 miles) of remaining range.

Continental’s specially developed tire achieved a rolling resistance of 4.9 kilograms per metric ton. That figure is approximately 25% below the threshold for the EU tire label’s highest class A rating.
According to Continental, approximately 20% of an electric vehicle’s propulsion energy goes toward overcoming tire rolling resistance. Reducing that resistance can help increase driving range.

“The record shows that increasing the range of electric cars does not necessarily require larger batteries. Significant opportunities lie in the successful interaction of all vehicle components. Tyres make a crucial contribution,” said Dr. Christian Strübel, Continental’s expert in rolling resistance for passenger car tires. “Together with Volkswagen, we’ve demonstrated what’s possible when vehicle, aerodynamics and tyre development are aligned from the very beginning.”
Continental Concept Tire Reduces Rolling Resistance
Tire rolling resistance directly affects electric vehicle energy consumption and driving range.

As a tire rotates, it deforms where it contacts the road surface. This deformation consumes energy that would otherwise be available for propulsion. Lower rolling resistance allows a vehicle to travel farther using the same battery charge.

Continental said it based its concept tire on the EcoContact 7, a production tire designed for low rolling resistance. The company modified the tire to meet Volkswagen’s specifications for the record attempt.
The resulting design reduces tire deformation during operation, helping lower energy consumption and increase range per battery charge.
Tire Construction and Manufacturing Process

Continental said it focused on two components to reduce rolling resistance: the sidewall design and tread compound. The concept tire uses the same sidewall design principle as the production EcoContact 7. This provides stability without increasing rolling resistance.
Continental said it also tailored the tread compound to work with the tire’s other components. Together with the carcass and tread pattern, the compound helps minimize energy losses during rotation.
The manufacturing process provides another opportunity to reduce rolling resistance.
During vulcanization, manufacturers use heat and pressure to harden the initially soft green tire in a mold. Conventional production typically heats the tire uniformly.

For the concept tire, Continental said it applied different temperatures to individual tire areas. The tread and sidewall undergo different curing conditions, allowing engineers to optimize their properties separately.
For the tread, this process contributes to lower rolling resistance.

Continental also said it designed the concept tire to minimize rolling noise. Engineers varied the spacing and angles of the tread blocks to create sounds that partially overlap and cancel each other.

The principle is similar to noise-canceling headphones and helps reduce the tire noise experienced inside the vehicle. This is particularly relevant for electric vehicles, where tire noise becomes more noticeable without an internal combustion engine.
Continental and Volkswagen Collaborate on Tire Development
Volkswagen’s Mission Efficiency concept is based on the ID. Polo, which uses Continental’s EcoContact 7 as standard equipment.
For the record project, Continental said it worked with Volkswagen’s vehicle and aerodynamics engineers from an early development stage.
The teams coordinated tire, vehicle and aerodynamic development to improve overall efficiency.
The collaboration also included visual design. Continental incorporated color accents and styling elements from the Mission Efficiency concept into the tire’s sidewall.
Volkswagen Mission Efficiency Sets Three Records
The Mission Efficiency established three records during its long-distance drive:
- Aerodynamics: Most aerodynamic near-production vehicle, with a drag coefficient (Cd) of 0.158.
- Energy efficiency: Most efficient four-seat electric vehicle in its class during a single drive under controlled conditions.
- Long-distance efficiency: Most economical near-production four-seat electric vehicle on an officially documented long-distance drive under real-world conditions.
The vehicle featured an aerodynamically optimized shape and additional solutions to improve airflow.
Volkswagen based the Mission Efficiency on production components from the ID. Polo, including its battery and drivetrain.
The record drive demonstrated efficiency improvements through targeted changes to existing electric vehicle technologies under real-world, long-distance driving conditions.

articles.title: The Downside of Regenerative Braking
articles.author: Joe Keene

paras.en: Regenerative braking allows electric vehicles to recover energy during deceleration. Instead of converting all vehicle momentum into heat at the brake rotors, the electric motor acts as a generator. This slows the vehicle while returning some energy to the battery.
The process can significantly reduce the use of conventional friction brakes. However, reduced brake usage can also create maintenance challenges involving corrosion and component operation.
On conventional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, brake pads regularly contact the rotors during braking. This friction helps remove light surface corrosion from the rotor faces.
EVs with aggressive regenerative braking may use their friction brakes less frequently. Exposure to moisture, road salt and humidity can then allow corrosion to develop on the rotor surfaces.
EV Regenerative Braking and Rotor Corrosion
Light surface rust is not necessarily a problem because normal brake applications can remove it. However, corrosion can progress when friction brakes are not used regularly.
Over time, heavier rust, pitting and scaling can develop on the rotors. Once the rotor surfaces deteriorate significantly, normal brake applications may not restore their condition.
Reduced friction brake usage can also extend brake pad life. However, brake components can develop problems unrelated to friction material wear.

Corrosion may form around brake pad hardware, caliper brackets, slide pins and other components. Pads can become restricted in their brackets, while caliper components may develop problems from limited movement.
As a result, brake components may require replacement because of corrosion or restricted movement rather than normal wear.
How Regenerative and Friction Braking Work Together
Electric vehicles still require conventional hydraulic friction brakes to maintain stopping performance.

Regenerative braking may become reduced or unavailable under certain operating conditions. These include a fully charged battery, very cold battery temperatures, vehicle stability control intervention or certain system faults.
EV braking systems blend regenerative braking with conventional hydraulic friction braking to provide the stopping performance drivers expect.
This makes conventional brake system condition an important consideration, even when regenerative braking reduces normal friction brake usage.
EV Brake Inspection and Maintenance Considerations
Technicians should account for reduced friction brake usage when inspecting electric vehicle braking systems.
Measuring brake pad thickness alone may not provide a complete picture of component condition.

EV regenerative braking improves efficiency by recovering energy and can substantially extend brake pad life. However, reduced friction brake usage can also increase the potential for corrosion and restricted component movement.
Brake condition assessments should account for both friction material wear and the effects of limited brake usage.

articles.author: Kevin Linger

The Career Driver driver agent is available through the Career Driver mobile app and is designed to act on a driver’s behalf rather than simply return job listings or answer questions.

“Our partnership with Career Driver started with a shared vision for creating a better mobile experience for drivers, but we’ve always seen the opportunity to build something much bigger together,” said Lori Furnell, president of Truck Drivers USA.
Drivers can use the agent to identify job opportunities and take the next step toward connecting with an employer.

articles.author: Kevin Linger

paras.en: The American Transportation Research Institute (ATRI) elected Ben McLean as ATRI board chairman. He will lead the research organization’s 13-member board.
The institute also appointed Ben Banks, president of TCW, and Nathan Meisgeier, president and chief legal officer of Werner Enterprises.
McLean, CEO of Ruan Transportation Management Systems, succeeds Derek Leathers, chairman and CEO of Werner Enterprises. Leathers is completing four years as ATRI chair.

“We are excited to have Ben McLean lead the ATRI Board,” said Rebecca Brewster, ATRI president and COO. “His commitment to research excellence and innovation will help drive the Institute forward for years to come. We also want to thank Derek Leathers for his dedicated service as Chairman and welcome Ben Banks and Nathan Meisgeier to the Board. Their extensive industry experience and insights will be tremendous assets to ATRI as we continue advancing our research mission.”
Board Members Bring Research and Fleet Leadership Experience

The new ATRI board chairman joined the board in October 2017. McLean has served as Ruan’s CEO since 2015, after joining the carrier in 2007. His previous positions included chief operating officer and chief information officer.

Banks has worked at TCW for more than 15 years. He previously served as a member and chair of ATRI’s Research Advisory Committee and is a 2018 graduate of the American Trucking Associations’ LEAD program.

Meisgeier has served as Werner’s president and chief legal officer since January 2024 and also serves as chief of staff. He joined the company in 2005, and his responsibilities include legal, safety, risk, human resources, recruiting, and government affairs.
He also chairs the American Trucking Associations’ Legal Reform Advisory Committee and serves on its Litigation Center board.

By continuing to identify common failure points and develop better repair solutions, we create new opportunities for our customers while helping them deliver greater value to the technicians and vehicle owners they serve.”

The original equipment oil filter housing on certain Genesis, Hyundai and Kia vehicles uses plastic that can warp. Prolonged exposure to heat and chemicals under the hood can cause the plastic to degrade. Over time, the housing can leak oil or crack.

The 926-611 builds on the performance of Dorman’s patented 926-959 aluminum oil filter housing. That product serves a wide range of Chrysler, Dodge, Jeep, Ram and Volkswagen vehicles.

Dorman has expanded its portfolio of oil filter housings, adapters, coolers, assemblies and seals. The product line addresses common original equipment failure points and aims to help technicians avoid repeat repairs.

articles.title: NAPA Opens First Highly Automated Reverse Logistics Center
articles.author: Mary DellaValle

paras.en: NAPA recently celebrated the grand opening of its York Reverse Logistics Center (RLC), marking the debut of the first highly automated facility of its kind within the NAPA network and an important milestone in the company’s ongoing supply chain transformation.

The 400,000-square-foot center combines more than 100 robots and advanced automation technology with a skilled local workforce to process returns, cores and inventory for redistribution across the NAPA Northeast distribution network.

The center began operations earlier this year and is designed to accelerate returns processing, helping get parts back into inventory faster and improving availability for NAPA stores, repair professionals and their customers, the company said. The new facility, which can support 250,000 unique SKUs, is expected to reduce the time needed to prepare inventory for redistribution by 43% and support inventory accuracy up to 99.5%.

Leaders from NAPA and corporate parent Genuine Parts Company (GPC) were joined by York Mayor Sandie Walker, state and local elected officials, the York County Economic Alliance, community partners and teammates for a ribbon-cutting ceremony and tours of the facility at 500 Willow Springs Lane.

“York is the first step in a broader modernization of the NAPA supply chain,” said Justin Ducharme, executive vice president, supply chain, NAPA. “By combining innovative technology with the expertise of our teammates, we’re creating a more efficient operation that helps keep parts moving to the customers and repair professionals who rely on us every day.”

During the ceremony, the GPC Foundation presented a $2,500 Good Neighbor grant to United Way of York County. The grant supports the foundation’s mobility priority and reflects a shared belief that reliable transportation opens access to jobs, health care and stronger family life.

As the first highly automated reverse logistics center within the NAPA network, RLC represents an important milestone in the company’s efforts to enhance operational capabilities and support the growing needs of customers across the Northeast, the company said.

articles.title: Romans carefully dismantled statue of emperor when they withdrew from Scotland 1,800 years ago, leaving only his foot behind
articles.author: Kristina Killgrove

paras.en: All that remains of a larger-than-life statue of the Roman emperor Antoninus Pius once erected in Scotland is a lower right leg. Experts have now reconstructed what the entire sculpture looked like but are still unsure why it was carefully dismantled over 1,800 years ago.

The gold-covered bronze foot and calf, also known as the Milsington leg, was discovered in a bog in 1820, according to a Nov. 12 statement from National Museums Scotland. It is the only example of a monumental Roman emperor statue ever found in Scotland and was likely made around A.D. 140.

Initially, experts thought the bronze statue had been looted from York, England, which was founded by the Romans in A.D. 71 as the town of Eboracum. But as research into the Roman frontier advanced over the years, it became clear that equestrian statues were often set up in forts along the border of the Roman Empire.
This lower leg, experts now believe, originally came from an equestrian statue of Emperor Antoninus Pius that was similar to the famous statue of Marcus Aurelius in Rome.

Antoninus Pius was Roman emperor from A.D. 138 to 161, succeeding Hadrian, who had built an enormous wall to defend the northernmost limit of the Roman Empire. To add to Rome's territory, Antoninus Pius directed the imperial governor of Roman Britain to move north, invade southern Scotland and build a second wall, called the Antonine Wall. But that wall was left undefended after Antoninus Pius died, and the Romans retreated from Scotland.

During that retreat, the Romans may have dismantled any valuable statues that they had set up, according to the statement. An examination of the Milsington leg ahead of a new exhibition showed that the bronze had no cut marks, suggesting it was removed carefully and not "brutally hacked off."

"This contrasts with examples of statues being deliberately destroyed after a battle, when an emperor's memory was condemned, or when they were chopped up for scrap," according to National Museums Scotland.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
With the Scottish provenance firmly established, National Museums Scotland curators were able to learn more about Antoninus Pius and his approach to imperial expansion.

"This really turns on its head our understanding of Rome's second attempt at conquering Scotland," Fraser Hunter, principal curator of prehistoric art and Roman archaeology at National Museums Scotland, said in the statement. "This was a big deal for the Emperor, something which was worth celebrating."

But while the boot-clad bronze leg provides a glimpse into the monuments that may have graced southern Scotland nearly two millennia ago, it raises an important question for Hunter: Where is the rest of the statue?

The Milsington leg, the Inveresk Mithras altars and other Roman-period finds are on display beginning Nov. 14 in the exhibit "Roman Scotland: Life on the Edge of Empire" at the National Museum of Scotland.
From Augustus to Nero, see how much you know about ancient Rome's famous leaders with our Roman emperor quiz!

Kristina Killgrove is a staff writer at Live Science with a focus on archaeology and paleoanthropology news. Her articles have also appeared in venues such as Forbes, Smithsonian, and Mental Floss. Kristina holds a Ph.D. in biological anthropology and an M.A. in classical archaeology from the University of North Carolina, as well as a B.A. in Latin from the University of Virginia, and she was formerly a university professor and researcher. She has received awards from the Society for American Archaeology and the American Anthropological Association for her science writing.

articles.title: 'Godless' founder of utilitarianism had severe dental problems and was in 'excruciating pain,' CT scans of his severed head reveal
articles.author: Tom Metcalfe

paras.en: The great and "godless" English philosopher Jeremy Bentham, whose remains have been on display at a U.K. university for over 150 years, suffered from severe dental problems, according to X-ray scans of his skull.

The scans were conducted with CT (computed tomography) scanning equipment to create a digital 3D model of his head and highlight Bentham's lengthy "presence" at University College London (UCL) as it celebrates its 200th anniversary.

The scans revealed that Bentham was missing many teeth and had advanced arthritis in his lower jaw when he died of natural causes at the age of 84. During the scanning process, project leader Tannis Davidson, curator of UCL's Grant Museum of Zoology, saw how thin the jawbone had become. "He must have been in excruciating pain," she told Live Science.

Bentham's utilitarian philosophy inspired UCL's founders; it was only the third university in England, after Oxford and Cambridge, which was founded as London University in 1826 and opened to students in 1828.

As a young man, Bentham had declared that he would donate his body to science after his death. This was a radical idea at the time; in the U.K., dissection after death was looked down upon, even if it was for scientific purposes, and it was reserved for the worst criminals. After Bentham died in 1832, his remains were fashioned into an auto-icon — a supposed replica of himself — to memorialize him in the way a tombstone might, Davidson said.
Except for brief visits across Europe and to the Met Breuer in New York City, this auto-icon has been in a display case at UCL since the 1850s, where it can be seen by students as they pass by.

To make the auto-icon (which is not a mummy), Bentham's body was dissected and studied. Then, his skeleton was dressed in his clothes, which were padded with straw. His severed head was badly disfigured during an attempt to preserve it with sulfuric acid, so a wax reconstruction based on paintings and death masks was attached to the body.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

Bentham's real head was displayed at the feet of the clothed skeleton that had a lifelike wax head; the real head's eyes were replaced with highly detailed glass eyes, which can be seen in the scans. According to UCL lore, the real head was stolen in 1975 and held ransom for a few days by rivals from King's College London, after which it was locked away.

Davidson explained that Bentham had coined the term "auto-icon" to mean "self-representation" and was setting an example for others. "He imagined a future where people were making auto-icons to keep their dead relatives around," she said.

The CT scans of the real head show that Bentham had dental damage and jaw arthritis, and that his brain had been removed before it was preserved—although some of his dura mater, a layer of connective tissue that covers the brain and spinal cord, was preserved. Davidson said the brain extraction was done to keep with Bentham's instructions that his head be mummified in the same way as Māori heads, which had their brains removed. The scanning process is shown in a short film called "Bentham Revealed."
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Bentham wrote about his dental problems several times, Davidson said, but it is not clear if he understood that he also had severe arthritis in his lower jaw, which must have made the problems with his teeth much more painful. In addition, modern ideas about cleaning teeth had not been established by Bentham's time. "Dentistry 200 years ago was a very different kettle of fish than it is today," Davidson said.

Bentham was a polymath who hoped to improve the lives of ordinary people through social reform. He wrote extensively about subjects as varied as law, economics, education and animal rights, and he believed that society could be engineered to produce better outcomes through legislation and the objective measurement of "utility."

His most famous idea was the panopticon in 1791, a ring-shaped prison with one warden to watch all of the prisoners, which he proposed as a humane alternative to Australia's penal colonies. Today, however, it is a symbol of state control and surveillance. Bentham also invented a "felicific calculus" to numerically assess the benefits and drawbacks of any given action, based on variables like its intensity, duration, certainty, purity and extent.
Bentham's philosophy put him at odds with the established Church of England; he called himself an "unbeliever," while critics called him "godless."

This rift with the church may have played a part in Bentham's wishes for his remains. Davidson suggested that the auto-icon may have been a means for Bentham to avoid being buried with traditional Anglican rites. "Maybe this was a way he could 'stick it to them' a little bit," she said.

Tom Metcalfe is a freelance journalist and regular Live Science contributor who is based in London in the United Kingdom. Tom writes mainly about science, space, archaeology, the Earth and the oceans. He has also written for the BBC, NBC News, National Geographic, Scientific American, Air & Space, and many others.

articles.title: Scientists discover two adorable species of howler monkey in the Amazon — and they're already endangered
articles.author: Sascha Pare

paras.en: Scientists have identified two newfound species of howler monkey in the Amazon rainforest. The discoveries could redraw branches of these primates' evolutionary tree, a new study shows.

The new species were named Alouatta iroi and Alouatta matogrossensis. The adorable creatures have bushy beards, winsome expressions and bright red fur. Their identification raises the number of known howler monkey species to 16, researchers said in a statement.

"Our study shows that the Amazon still holds remarkable biological secrets, even among well-known animals such as howler monkeys," study first author Romina Batista, a biodiversity scientist at the University of Gothenburg in Sweden and the University of Salford in the U.K., said in the statement.
One of the newfound species, A. matogrossensis, is probably on the brink of extinction. The other newfound species faces threats from a planned dam on the Rio Branco River, according to the study.

In addition to identifying the new species, the study, published Oct. 30 in the journal Communications Biology, used genetic evidence to understand when howler monkeys spread out and diversified. The researchers analyzed the genomes of 11 howler monkey species living in South and Central America, combining existing DNA datasets with new genomic information from specimens in Brazilian zoological collections.
Overall, the genetic data confirmed that howler monkeys diverged from close relatives between 19 million and 13.5 million years ago. But the analysis changed the picture of more recent evolution.

For instance, the team argued that the Tapajós red-handed howler (A. tapajozensis) and the Amazonian black howler (A. nigerrima) are not as closely related as scientists previously thought. The researchers also said that the Trinidad howler (A. insulanus), whose status has been unclear, should be confirmed as a separate species.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

"This discovery comes at a critical time, as increasing deforestation, climate change and habitat loss threaten many Amazonian species before they are fully understood or even discovered by science," study co-author Jean Boubli, a professor and chair of primate ecology and evolution at the University of Salford in the U.K., said in the statement.

The scientists found that natural barriers such as the Amazon River, the Xingu River and the Branco River drove many howler monkeys to develop separately. Researchers believe that howler monkeys can swim across small waterways, but big rivers block groups from mixing, which led to different traits and species evolving over time. Natural barriers are a common reason why species emerge in the Amazon, the researchers noted in the study.

articles.title: This Four-Person NASA Crew Spent Over a Year on 'Mars.' Here's What They Did for 378 Days in a Simulated Martian Habitat

paras.en: On October 31, four NASA crewmembers returned from “Mars.” Not the actual Red Planet, of course, but a 3D-printed Mars habitat in Houston where the three men and one woman lived for 378 days.

Now, the Mars analog astronauts—Ross Elder, Ellen Ellis, James Spicer and Matthew Montgomery—have started telling the world what took place after they disappeared into NASA’s Mars Dune Alpha habitat at the Johnson Space Center on October 19, 2025, for the agency’s second Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) mission.

The mission aimed to test the kinds of physical and mental conditions that a team of Mars explorers would endure on the Red Planet, including long-term isolation, disrupted communication with people on Earth and food cultivation. The habitat includes both a base and a mock outdoor environment, so the crew could practice Marswalks.

“For more than a year, they have lived in an isolated environment, conducting critical research and helping us better understand what it will take to send humans to Mars,” Vanessa Wyche, director of NASA’s Johnson Space Center, said during a livestream, just before the crew emerged. “Inside just 1,700 square feet, they managed to live with limited resources. They maintained their habitat. They grew crops, and they carried out simulated Mars operations.”

After the speech, NASA astronaut Jack Hathaway, who had just completed a mission at the International Space Station, knocked on the door to the Mars habitat, called out “trick or treat” and opened it to reveal the crew’s smiling faces. Since then, the analog astronauts have been participating in post-mission evaluations and debriefs that, along with the data collected during their year in the simulated environment, will help inform future missions to Mars and those closer to home, per a NASA statement.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “Most days, we had things that were scheduled, from maintenance and science and engineering activities and some operational activities. So, we often do extravehicular activities, also known as EVAs or spacewalks,” Elder, who was the mission’s commander and test pilot, tells CNN News Central. “We would do drone and rover operations where we control certain equipment outside of the habitat, and we would practice additional data collection for both human health and behavioral sciences.”

Each team member brought unique expertise to the mission. Elder was an experimental test pilot at the U.S. Air Force. Ellis, the mission’s medical officer and tactical thinker, is a U.S. Space Force officer. Spicer was the flight engineer and systems specialist, and he has experience in satellite communications and spacecraft development. Montgomery’s diverse background in hardware engineering, robotics, technology startups and independent films made him the “Swiss Army knife of crewmates;” he served as the mission’s science officer and versatile engineer.

paras.en: Quick fact: When was the first CHAPEA mission?

The first mission of this kind also lasted 378 days, during which crewmembers Kelly Haston, Ross Brockwell, Nathan Jones and Anca Selariu entered the Mars Dune Alpha habitat on June 25, 2023, and emerged on July 6, 2024.

Elder tells Fox News that combining their skills created “magic.” But that didn’t happen by accident; the selection process lasted about a year and a half and included personality evaluations by NASA psychologists, Montgomery tells the outlet. What’s more, they got to practice before entering the habitat.

“The crew spent a lot of time together prior to the mission, so we got to work on our teamwork and build relationships,” Montgomery tells Nature’s Kaia Glickman, including during a winter camping expedition that overlapped with a blizzard. “These high-pressure scenarios set a nice foundation for pre-training, where we spent five weeks together before going into isolation. Through all of those tools that we built, we had a really good dynamic as a team inside of the habitat, and conflict was very minimal.”

paras.en: Montgomery and his crewmates could still speak with mission control, but the communication system intentionally mimicked delays that would occur on a real Mars mission. That meant messages could take up to 22 minutes to deliver, and the team even had to deal with a planned two-week communication blackout. Future travelers to Mars will experience this communications barrier when Earth and the Red Planet are temporarily on opposite sides of the sun, blocking radio signals from traveling between the planets, according to Nature.
