articles.title: Archaeologists in England Discovered 8,000 Roman-Era Frog Bones in a Single Ditch. They Just Solved the Mystery of How the Amphibians Ended Up There

paras.en: Between 2016 and 2022, archaeologists conducting excavations along a planned stretch of England’s A14 highway unearthed an array of astonishing discoveries, including a Roman amulet carved to resemble the mythical Gorgon Medusa, the earliest physical evidence of beer production in Britain and an Iron Age comb crafted from a human skull.

Comprising more than 280,000 artifacts, the finds—uncovered between modern-day Cambridge and Huntingdon—shed light on life in the region over roughly 12,000 years. But some discoveries raised more questions than answers: Why, for example, did a single ditch at the Bar Hill site in rural Cambridgeshire contain some 8,000 amphibian bones?

As Vicki Ewens, a senior zooarchaeologist at the Museum of London Archaeology (MOLA), told the Observer’s Dalya Alberge in 2022, “In my experience, mainly working on sites from London, we don’t get that many frogs. To have so many bones coming from one ditch is extraordinary.”

Ewens and her colleagues outlined several possible explanations for the unusual cache. Perhaps the amphibians fell into the ditch (also described as a gully) and found themselves trapped. Or maybe they succumbed to extreme cold during their wintertime hibernation. Alternatively, they could have served as the centerpiece of a meal—or several—enjoyed by Iron Age humans, although the absence of cut marks on the bones rendered this scenario unlikely.

Four years after MOLA first announced the find, experts have finally solved the mystery of the ancient animal cemetery. Based on a groundbreaking analysis of amphibian arm bones, researchers led by Ewens and Paul Clarkson, an archaeologist at England’s Bournemouth University, concluded that most of the frogs whose remains were found in the ditch died young, eaten by birds of prey such as short-eared owls and hen harriers in the second or third century C.E., during Britain’s Roman era.

A combination of environmental factors and human activity produced ideal conditions for this avian feast to unfold over a relatively short timeframe. As the authors write in the journal Environmental Archaeology, water levels in the Fens—the marshy wetland that houses the gully—retreated during the Roman period, enabling frogs in drying-out ponds to reproduce at a faster rate. When birds in search of their next meal arrived, they had no trouble spotting their prey: Locals had felled the trees in the area to make way for grazing livestock, leaving the amphibians with limited woodland protection from aerial predators.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - All toads are frogs, but not all frogs are toads. Both animals belong to the Anura order, meaning they are amphibians that lack tails.

- According to the University of Michigan’s Animal Diversity Web database, “There is no scientific distinction between ‘frogs’ and ‘toads,’ although most anurans are usually referred to as one or the other.”

“We don’t often get an owl’s eye view of what it was like in the past from archaeological sites,” Clarkson says in a statement. “These bones not only tell us about life for people living near the Roman Fens, but they also give insights into the natural world—what wild animals were getting up to in the past, and what life was like for them.”

The majority of the bones belonged to frogs and toads (specifically common frogs), but shrews, voles and mice were also present in the assemblage. The remains represented no fewer than 469 individual animals.

To estimate the frogs’ ages at their time of death, the researchers measured the amphibians’ distal humeri, or arm bones—a method previously described by Clarkson and several co-authors in a 2025 paper. According to the study, the team determined that a large number of the frogs died in either their first or second year of life, during a “short, intensive predation event” spanning autumn to the following spring, “probably along migration routes to and from hibernation sites.” An abundance of frogs likely attracted “local and migrant predators to the area to feed on them and also, coincidentally, on other locally available prey, such as voles, insectivores, birds and fish.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Based on breakage patterns and physical traces of digestion seen on the bones, the paper’s authors ruled out several species that typically prey on amphibians, including otters, gray herons and grass snakes. Instead, they suggest that the “lightly digested and relatively unbroken bones” are more consistent with medium-sized birds such as short-eared owls.

Initially, the archaeologists identified the gully as a roundhouse in an enclosure dating to Britain’s Iron Age, which began around 750 B.C.E. and ended with the Roman invasion in 43 C.E. But radiocarbon dating of the bones shifted this timeline forward by several hundred years.

How did humans fit into this puzzle? Although the researchers considered the possibility that ancient people intentionally deposited the bones in the ditch, the only evidence for this scenario was the presence of a Roman-era brooch among the animal remains. In all likelihood, the authors argue in the paper, the mass predation event only took place because humans weren’t in the area at the time: Short-eared owls “only choose quiet roosting sites, so people must have rarely visited this area, particularly with dogs.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Why locals steered clear of this specific spot in the autumn and winter remains unclear, but the scientists posit that “the most probable explanation is seasonal movement of livestock.” Avoidance tied to social or ritual reasons is also possible.

“I had so many theories as to why such [a] large collection of frog bones were recovered from this small feature,” Ewens says in the statement. “This research shows how even the smallest animal recovered on a site can help us to understand not only past environmental conditions but human activity within a wider landscape.”

articles.title: Thawing Permafrost May Have Created a New Type of Landslide, Which Could Become More Common as the World Warms

paras.en: In 2017 and 2018, a pair of strange landslides moved huge masses of rock and dirt in Canada’s Northwest Territories. The events occurred in the central Mackenzie Valley, and one of them even dammed a river and created a lake.

The two natural disasters are part of a new class of landslides scientists are calling “permafrost detachment slides” in a study published in the journal Geophysical Research Letters in September. They may have been partially triggered by severe wildfires that occurred in 1995, which destabilized the ground and allowed the base of the permafrost to thaw. What’s more, these events may become more common as the planet continues to warm.

“It’s a very dramatic manifestation of the changing climate,” says study co-author Joseph Young, a geoscientist who conducted the work at the University of Alberta in Canada, to Matt Simon at Grist. “They’ve only started happening in the last 10, 15 years, and it’s a very drastic and abrupt change in the landscape.”

Young and his colleagues began the study after seeing something strange in the Northwest Territories in 2019. While conducting field research, they spotted large landslide scars in valleys that they knew were stable permafrost, or permanently frozen earth, reports Stephanie Pappas for Live Science.

To better understand what happened, the team homed in on two major events: the Johnson River slide in August 2017 that moved about 4.5 million cubic meters of dirt and rock, and the Redstone River slide in August 2018 that sent roughly 18 million cubic meters of debris tumbling down. Satellite imagery captured between 1980 and 2020 and field studies revealed some odd characteristics, the team found.

“Typically with permafrost, everything just thaws and melts in a slurry and moves like a mud downslope,” Young tells Live Science. “But with these large landslides, we found blocks of frozen material in the debris.”

The team monitored the temperature near the 1995 burn area near the slides and, for comparison, undisturbed forest from September 2020 to August 2022. Their data went into computer simulations, which allowed the researchers to investigate how the wildfires decades earlier may have affected the region.

Their resulting hypothesis? The fires that swept through the landscape burned off the vegetation that usually keeps the permafrost cool on sunny days. “After about 20 years or so, that thermal signature from the burned forest can reach the base of permafrost,” Young tells Grist. “It’s slight, but it’s there.”

As the frozen ground warmed, it weakened and formed cracks, allowing water to seep in. That allowed the permafrost to thaw even more, destabilizing its bottom layers. Eventually, that caused the ground to detach and created the two landslides at the center of the study. They’re among more than 150 permafrost landslides in the area that happened around two decades after the severe wildfires, meaning the newly proposed mechanism could have contributed to many of these catastrophic events.

The findings suggest scientists need to better study what’s happening below the surface of permafrost regions, says Dmitry Nicolsky, a geophysicist at the University of Alaska Fairbanks who wasn’t involved in the work, to Nikk Ogasa at Science News. “We don’t know how [the ground] will move—it might go slowly or it might go catastrophically.”
Thankfully, Young says experts can look out for signs of an impending permafrost detachment slide and predict when it’s going to happen.

“That’s kind of the silver lining,” he tells Julia Parrish at the CBC. “It doesn’t just happen overnight; it kind of happens in a more progressive manner over the course of about 20 years after a fire, where you get a slow downslope movement of these slopes.”

articles.title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
articles.author: Andrew Couts

paras.en: Sorry, Margaret, your email is working again.

After a widespread outage shut down Microsoft 365 services for businesses, governments, and tens of millions of other users around the world, the essential cloud services are now (mostly) back online, according to the company’s status page.

The outage debacle began around lunchtime on the East Coast on Thursday, with users reporting Outlook outages to the service-tracking website Downdetector just after 12 pm ET. Within the hour, Microsoft said it was investigating reports of an outage that at the time was limited to North America. It quickly spread to impact more than 70 countries around the world.

The full cause of Microsoft’s unprecedented outage remains unknown, but the company repeatedly ruled out a cyberattack as the cause in statements to its status page. It is also ruling out AI or AI agents playing a role in the debacle.

“We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services,” a Microsoft spokesperson says in a statement. “This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.”
The company has promised a “full post-incident report” after it has fully reviewed what went wrong.

As Outlook, Teams, Copilot, and other Microsoft 365 systems come back online, users will likely see their inboxes turn into a mess. “You're probably going to get a lot of notifications when things come back,” says Jonathan Leitschuh, an independent researcher.

Microsoft said it had increased the queue time for emails to 48 hours in an attempt to ensure that every message that people tried to send while its systems were down gets delivered. Leitschuh points out that, even with the bulk of systems restored, users may receive “a flood of notifications a few hours down the pike” as subsystems come back online.

The total impact of the Microsoft outage may never be fully known, but it’s safe to say it’s already significant. Governments from Japan to the United States reported disruptions to a bevy of functions. Airlines reported problems with their ability to communicate with customers. Many law enforcement and emergency services ground to a halt. And hospitals reported widespread interruptions to their operations.

Ultimately, the episode serves as a reminder of the risks involved when the whole world relies on a single company for a critical service. “We're very interdependent on these systems in modern life,” says Leitschuh. Next time, delayed emails may be the least of our worries.

articles.title: Taylor Swift couldn't write 'Toy Story 5' song 'until I was in my 30s'

paras.en: LOS ANGELES, Nov. 13 (UPI) -- Taylor Swift said her song from Toy Story 5, "I Knew It, I Knew You," reflected maturity she's come to in her own life. The song plays at the end of the film and is on the soundtrack.
In Toy Story 5Joan Cusack) visits the home where her former owner, Emily, grew up. A new family, with a young daughter Blaze (Mykal-Michelle Harris), lives there now.

In a recent Zoom press conference with the Critics Choice Association, Swift, 36, described her process of writing the song with Jack Antonoff. She responded to the way the film gave Jessie closure over her heartbreak from 1999's Toy Story 2.

"I was so struck by the lessons that Jessie learned," Swift said. "I think that resonated with me because they were lessons I learned in my life. Maybe I wouldn't be able to write this song until I was in my 30s. It takes a long time to process and perceive memory with acceptance."
Without spoiling Jessie's discovery for viewers yet to watch the latest film, which is now on home video, she finds clues to Emily's life without her.

"This specific type of gratitude that this song is about, it just feels like it's something I've arrived at more recently in my life," Swift said. "I don't think I was ready to write about it in this type of way until I saw Jessie experience it."

In Toy Story 2, Woody the cowboy (Tom Hanks) met Jessie when he discovered he was part of a collectible Woody's Roundup set. Jessie told him the story of Emily outgrowing her and donating her to charity.
Jessie has remained a part of Woody's gang through the Toy Story sequels. Only in Toy Story 5 does she find some evidence that Emily did not just forget about her toy. Swift could relate.

"There's a weight lifted because you realize you don't have to carry that particular thing around anymore," she said. "It took me a while to realize how to release certain things from the load you drag around. I happened to see the movie at the perfect time to write this."
As much as she related to Jessie, Swift also felt relief writing a song in her character. Many of Swift's own songs are autobiographical.

"In another way there is a pressure release valve of not having to write about my personal life," Swift said. "Being able to absorb myself in a story that I wasn't just watching unfold when I watched Toy Story 5, I've been watching this story unfold since I was 5."

The original Toy Story came out in November 1995. Toy Story 2 was 1999. Sarah McLachlan sang "When She Loved Me" about Jessie remembering Emily's childhood, and longing for the days when she loved her.

"That song is so perfect and devastating that there are times that I will just think about it and feel like I'm gonna cry," Swift said. "I don't even need to hear it to feel that way. It's so potent and it's so powerful. It's really sorrow and heartbreak and grief in its purest form."

Swift's song was able to offer healing to Jessie, and viewers who have remained devastated by Toy Story 2 since the last century. Jessie cannot go back to being Emily's toy, but she learns she made a positive impact on Emily's adult life.
"You can be there for someone for a time in their lives and make an impact and that can be enough to really mean something," Swift said. "I wanted to hint at 'When She Loved Me' and then heal it."
Randy Newman has been the composer and songwriter for the entire Toy Story franchise. His original song "You've Got a Friend In Me" has been the theme for the whole series.

So Swift and Antonoff wanted to honor Newman and compose a song that fit with his franchise aesthetics. Swift described how that stretched her musically with chord progressions she would not typically write for herself.

"It's on that line of 'Life has ways of leaving those days behind,' I would have gone for an A minor," Swift said. "Instead we go to an A7 and then resolve in a D minor. It almost feels like you're about to modulate but you don't."
Swift also incorporated instruments she would not normally orchestrate, such a virginal harpsichord.

"We've got tenor sax, we've got baritone sax and they're playing in a way that is structured in a different way than we would normally do it," Swift said. "We would normally have very structured parts. Whereas in our world of trying to reach towards Randy Newman, we felt it could feel more like a jam band with individual players acting as characters."
Swift did want "I Knew It, I Knew You" to sound like country music, to go with Jessie.
"I think that her time on Woody's Roundup and her being a cowgirl, I know how to bring that in," Swift said. "We've got banjo, we've got mandolin, harmonica."

The musical arrangement came after the lyrics, Swift said. Lyrically, Swift said she wanted the words to have a double meaning, allegorically and literally. She explained the opening line as an example, "I knew you through the daze of the blades of the grass in summer."

"As an allegory, it's youth," she said. "It's the people who knew you when you didn't wear shoes very often. You were always outside, you were always covered in dirt, you were always sunburnt. That's a very specific version of you for someone to know."
Literally, the line describes the point of view of toys.
"When they're standing on the ground looking up at their kid, they're looking through the blades of grass because they're toys," she said

articles.title: Memo: White House staff must get approval to meet with lobbyists

paras.en: Nov. 13 (UPI) -- White House staff are no longer allowed to meet with lobbyists without prior approval, according to a memo by Chief of Staff Stephen Miller.
The memo, which was first obtained by Politico, went out Thursday night and says that staffers must get approval from the Office of White House Counsel before meeting with a lobbyist.

"No President in history has fought more relentlessly, selflessly or courageously for the American People than President Trump. Following his example, White House staff are expected to dedicate their time unwaveringly to the working people of the nation," the memo said.
Miller replaced former White House Chief of Staff Suzie Wiles after she was ousted three days after the midterm elections.
Miller isn't friendly with lobbyists, Politico said.

"The thing with Stephen [Miller] is, he's not someone that a lobbyist goes in and has to crack or try to win over," said Hunter Morgen, a lobbyist at Ballard Partners who worked with Miller during the first Trump administration. "He doesn't operate based on relationships. He operates based on policy outcomes that will advance the president's agenda."
A dozen lobbyists told Politico that Miller doesn't take relationship-based favors and isn't influenced on issues. He's driven by ideology and fiercely loyal to President Donald Trump, they said.

"Even in his deputy chief of staff role, he cared enough to be at Rose Garden dinners and Christmas parties and events that the donor community was invited to, like they do in all administrations," a Republican lobbyist who attends social events at White House, told Politico. "So it's not like he's an alien to that scene ... it's just going to be done differently."

"He's impossible to lobby, no one can do it, not even the people that you would think are closest," one of the lobbyists said. "I think he's more reasonable than he's being portrayed, but he's not swayed by lobbying."

articles.title: Arizona Cardinals sign tight end Elijah Higgins to 3-year extension

paras.en: Nov. 13 (UPI) -- The Arizona Cardinals signed tight end Elijah Higgins to a three-year extension, they announced Friday.
Higgins' agency, Equity Sports, said the pact is worth up to $26.8 million. The fourth-year tight end was entering the final season of his rookie contract.

Higgins, 26, was a sixth-round pick by the Miami Dolphins in the 2023 NFL Draft. The former collegiate wide receiver was waived by the Dolphins and claimed off waivers by the Cardinals in August of 2023.
Higgins caught 18 passes for 162 yards and a score through nine appearances this season. He hauled in 82 passes for 798 yards and four scores through his first four seasons for the Cardinals.
Higgins totaled career-highs in catches (30) and receiving yards (301) last season, when he appeared in 17 games for the Cardinals.
The Cardinals (3-6) will host the Los Angeles Rams (5-4) at 4:05 p.m. EST Sunday in Glendale, Ariz.

articles.title: Eisenkot Accuses Netanyahu of Fueling ‘Racist’ Hostility Against Arabs
articles.author: Adam Rasgon

paras.en: Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief who is trying to form the next Israeli government, accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday of fueling a “racist” campaign against the country’s Arab citizens, in some of the strongest public criticism of his rival’s attacks on the community.

The comments were made days after Mr. Netanyahu delivered a divisive speech to the opening session of Parliament, or the Knesset, in which he referred to Arab lawmakers as “terror supporters” and “haters of Israel.” Diplomats and analysts condemned the remarks as a brazen display of hatred and incitement against Arab citizens, who make up about 20 percent of the overall population, and voted in massive numbers in inconclusive elections last month.

“Since the beginning of the election campaign, they have been subjected to a racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimization, fueled by the outgoing prime minister and those around him for political purposes,” Mr. Eisenkot said in a statement on social media.
“Arab citizens of Israel are an integral part of the Israeli story,” he said, adding that it was wrong to malign an entire community.

“The attempt to marginalize them and vilify them collectively is a profound violation of the principles of statesmanship,” Mr. Eisenkot said. “It dishonors Israel’s Declaration of Independence and the values we take pride in as a Jewish and democratic state.”
The Declaration of Independence says all citizens have equal social and political rights “irrespective of religion, race or sex.”

articles.title: Europe Agrees on a Team to Represent It in Talks With Russia
articles.author: Jeanna Smialek

paras.en: European leaders have waited on the margins of negotiations to end Russia’s war in Ukraine for months, eyeing a seat at the table. They learned this week that they would get one, and simply needed to decide which official should sit in that chair.

European Union leaders concluded in Dublin on Friday that they will tap a group of major nations — Britain, France, Germany, Poland, and Italy — along with a representative from the E.U’s leadership arms, the European Council and European Commission.

In some ways, the choice of a crowd plays into jibes Americans have made about the continent’s indecisiveness: “If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiation,” Jared Kushner, President Trump’s son-in-law and a U.S. envoy, said earlier this week.

Europe’s failure to pick one negotiator leaves open the possibility that its fragmentation will diminish its influence. Even so, Europeans have underscored that they are a democracy of many nations, though, and that many voices must be represented.
“We decide on who represents us, and that is what we have done today,” said Ursula von der Leyen, the president of the European Commission.
“We need to work as a team,” António Costa, president of the European Union’s political leadership arm, said at a news conference on Friday, noting that America itself has two envoys.

articles.title: Microsoft’s Global Outage and Fixes: What We Know
articles.author: Michael Levenson

paras.en: Microsoft is reporting widespread improvements to its services after a global outage took them offline on Thursday, disrupting communications and work at schools, government agencies and offices around the world. The company, headquartered in Redmond, Wash., said on Friday that it was seeing “encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected infrastructure.”
“We remain focused on addressing residual impact and ensuring reliable service restoration,” the company added.
Here’s what to know as of Friday afternoon.

Outages started disrupting Microsoft tools and apps around noon Eastern time on Thursday and quickly spread to more than 70 countries and territories, affecting millions of users, according to Downdetector, an outage-tracking site.
Some of Microsoft’s most popular products, including the email manager Outlook, the workplace messaging and video calling app Teams and the artificial intelligence assistant Copilot, stopped working.

Microsoft said in a statement on Friday that “for now, we can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity.” It added that the problem was “a technical issue not related to cyber or A.I.” agents.
So why were Microsoft’s systems not working?
The company has yet to provide a clear answer, although it has promised to make public a full report that identifies the “root cause” of the outage.

articles.title: Gene Autry’s Guitar in Global Dispute
articles.author: Jessica Nicholson

paras.en: As programmers prepare Christmas playlists, the Gene Autry recordings “Rudolph, the Red-Nosed Reindeer” and “Here Comes Santa Claus (Down Santa Claus Lane)” are currently top of mind.

But a 1931 Autry recording – “That Silver-Haired Daddy of Mine,” which charted on Billboard’s all-genre hit parade in 1935 – is suddenly timely, as well, in a real-life detective story that’s erupted into a trans-Atlantic legal tiff.

A rare Martin OM-45 guitar, one of only 50 produced in the early-1930s, was found in a Swedish farmhouse among the inheritance a father left to his daughter when he died in February 2021. The guitar, it turns out, was likely owned by Autry and stolen from him in 1932. The exact journey the instrument took cannot be fully traced, but steps were taken somewhere in the past 90 years to conceal its identity. The process of uncovering the guitar’s authenticity and tracing its original ownership back to Autry, a Country Music Hall of Fame member who was an iconic singing cowboy during much of the 20th century, reads like a C.S.I. forensics drama, laid out in a four-part series by Swedish newspaper Göteborgs-Posten.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Autry’s widow, Jackie Autry, is now embroiled in a tug of war over the instrument, which she believes should be returned to the Autry Museum of the American West, a Los Angeles institution that documents cowboy and Native American history.
“I don’t have any of Gene’s guitars anymore,” Jackie told Göteborgs-Posten. “They’re all at the museum now because that’s where it belongs. It belongs to the public, not to me, not to her.”
“Her” would be the daughter of Owe Jakobsson, a Swedish woman named Sandra who was left in charge of her daddy’s estate after his death.

Owe had inherited the instrument from his father, Gunnar, who was an inventive repairman. The original guitar had amateur-grade modifications made to the neck and bridge, and Sandra received a $7,000 offer for the Martin when she was selling off pieces of the estate. Another potential buyer tipped her off that it was likely worth far more, and they discovered that even a modern replica is worth about $12,000. This guitar, which had all the earmarks of being an original, could be worth six figures.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Sandra took the instrument to a Stockholm guitar shop for restoration, and there, Leif Lundbäck discovered a name, Gene Autry, that had been covered with black paint. He also found a serial number when he detached the neck. The Martin company, they would discover, has documentation from several letters that Gene wrote in early 1932 that verify a connection.
The singer’s 1932 tax return, produced by the estate, indicates that a Martin guitar had been stolen from him in the fall, roughly nine months after his correspondence with Martin.

Autry’s widow, Jackie, offered $20,000 for the instrument after she was contacted. Sandra declined that figure, holding that the guitar has sentimental value because she had inherited it from her father. The two sides are at a stalemate – Autry has not increased her offer and told Göteborgs-Posten, “I don’t pay money to blackmailers.”

Sandra has been advised that the guitar is worth far more, and that Autry’s estate can afford it. The case is complicated by differing nuances in the laws of Sweden and the United States. “I’m the one who inherited it,” Sandra told Göteborgs-Posten. “So, with that said, I don’t think I’m being dishonest by wanting to keep it.

paras.en: From Rosalía’s wins for album of the year (Lux) and song of the year (“La Perla”) to Karol G’s best urban music album victory for Tropicoqueta, we’re looking back at the the 2026 Latin Grammy’s biggest wins, emotional speeches and standout performances. Watch Daddy Yankee’s person of the year tribute, Juanes and Carín León’s duet, and the moving José Alfredo Jiménez tribute featuring The Warning and Camila Fernández.

Karol G wins best urban music album for Tropicoqueta. Rosalía swept the top prize for song of the year for her catchy “La Perla” and crowned the night by conquering the coveted trophy for album of the year for Lux. Milo J took home the award for record of the year for “Niño.” Xavi wins his first Latin Grammy and dedicates it to Mexico. Also, newcomer Aria Vega won the coveted award for best new artist.

But let’s not forget these moments. Rosalía premiered the performance among the clouds of Lux alongside a dance cast of celestial aesthetics. articles.title: Eminem Joins IDK for Hard-Hitting J Dilla-Produced ‘Welcome’ as DMV Rapper Signs to Shady Records
articles.author: Michael Saponara

paras.en: With IDK joining the Shady Records roster, Eminem teamed up with the DMV-bred rapper for the fittingly titled new single “Welcome” on Friday (Nov. 13). The song also features production from the late, great Detroit beatmaker J Dilla.

Dilla sets the tone with his signature thumping drums and a menacing beat, which Em catches for a sinister chorus. “Welcome to the party where everybody dies at the end/ Move your body/ This is ’bout to be a homicide scene/ I think you are not mean when I scream,” he raps.

Slim Shady didn’t put a verse on “Welcome,” as it appears he wanted IDK to fully shine. The 34-year-old makes the most of his moment next to Em, showing off his dexterity as a rhymer. “We run this s–t, y’all n—as walk/ That’s why she twerkin’ all that a– when she take it off/ You— you know we talk that slick talk, that slick talk,” IDK raps while shrewdly sneaking in an interpolation of Future’s 2016 hit “Stick Talk.”
A black-and-white visual accompanied the release, which finds Eminem making an appearance alongside IDK. They take turns rapping in an apartment building hallway before IDK hits the town.

It’s a new era for IDK, who signed to Shady Records in partnership with Interscope Records. Hype for a possible Eminem collab surged earlier this week when the duo posed for a photo together in the studio on social media.

“When I first started working on this music, I remember looking up at my ceiling and saying, ‘Thank you’. I was speaking to Dilla because it felt like everything that could have been, in a way, started to clear itself organically,” IDK said in a statement. “I knew this was an important opportunity and a statement for hip-hop itself.”

He continued: “The first rap album I’ve ever owned was 50 Cent’s Get Rich or Die Tryin’. A Shady Records release. The first raps I made it a point to memorize were Eminem raps. I’ve been at it for some time now, so to be at the point in my journey seems surreal. I’m excited for this next chapter in my career.”

IDK released his e.t.d.s. (Even the Devil Smiles) project in January, which featured appearances from hip-hop heavyweights such as RZA, Pusha T, the late DMX and MF DOOM as well as Black Thought and No ID.

articles.title: When Kevin Feige Got Off to a Less-Than-Incredible Start at Marvel
articles.author: Lexy Perez

paras.en: The success that Marvel Studios honcho Kevin Feige has achieved over the two-plus decades since landing on The Hollywood Reporter‘s Next Gen list in 2003 would likely make any producer green with envy.

Boston-born and New Jersey-raised, Feige was rejected from USC film school five times before finally getting accepted. He later landed an unpaid internship with Superman director Richard Donner and his wife, producer Lauren Shuler Donner. Feige continued working as an assistant for Shuler Donner, leading him to earn an associate producer credit for Fox’s 2000 release X-Men. Feige’s passion for the company impressed Marvel Studios founder Avi Arad, who hired him to oversee other studios’ use of Marvel superheroes. Feige would later tell THR that, during his time as a Marvel Studios producer until he was named president of production in 2006, he would learn about the various productions and was “thinking always, ‘One day, if I’m in a position of power, I’ll do things this way; I’m going to not do things like that.’ ”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: At the time of his Next Gen selection in fall 2003, Feige was executive vp at Marvel Studios. He had also just executive produced Ang Lee’s Hulk, the Universal summer release that starred Eric Bana as physicist Bruce Banner, who transforms into his green-skinned alter ego when angered. Although THR‘s review praised the film for its “visual energy, genuine artistry and compelling human emotions,” it collected a modest $245 million globally against a $137 million budget. Three years later, Marvel Studios bought back the rights to the Hulk and released 2008’s Edward Norton-led movie The Incredible Hulk. Creative differences between Norton and the studio resulted in Mark Ruffalo taking over the role for 2012’s The Avengers. Ruffalo returns as the Hulk for Disney’s anticipated Avengers: Doomsday, which hits theaters Dec. 18 and stars an endless array of A-listers. The film is the 39th in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, which Feige helped launch in 2008 with Iron Man.

paras.en: Feige now serves as Marvel Studios president and Marvel chief creative officer — and in 2025, he gave an endowment to USC to establish the Kevin Feige Division of Film & Television Production. When asked to name his job’s greatest challenge on his Next Gen questionnaire, Feige replied: “Expanding and redefining the public’s perception of a ‘comic book movie.’ “

This set comes with the flexible LED light “canopy,” base unit, pillow, remote control, googles (to wear while under the lights) and a storage bag.

This device targets everything from skin health and hair loss to joint pain and recovery. The Helio Spark is also FDA-registered, and parent company Helio Cure says the panel is developed with a team of medical researchers to deliver “the wavelengths your body need most for healthy aging.”

articles.title: Hassett denies report he's leaving White House: 'Not true'

paras.en: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett on Friday poured cold water on a report that he's expected to leave the White House in the coming weeks.
paras.zh: 周五，国家经济委员会主任凯文·哈塞特（Kevin Hassett）对有关他预计将在未来几周内离开白宫的报道泼了冷水。

paras.en: That report is "not true," Hassett told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a text message.
paras.zh: 哈塞特在发给CNBC的埃蒙·贾弗斯（Eamon Javers）的短信中表示，该报道“不属实”。

paras.en: Semafor reported earlier Friday afternoon that Hassett "has been inquiring about roles outside the administration," even before Republicans' drubbing in last week's midterm election.
paras.zh: Semafor在周五下午早些时候报道称，早在共和党在上周的中期选举中惨败之前，哈塞特“就在打听政府以外的职位”。

paras.en: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, and his counselor David Zervos, are among the names being floated to replace Hassett, according to Semafor, which cited unnamed people familiar with his plans.
paras.zh: 据Semafor援引知情人士透露，财政部长斯科特·贝森特及其顾问大卫·泽沃斯是接替哈塞特的候选人之一。

paras.en: But a White House official told CNBC in a statement later Friday, "There is no factual basis for this reporting."
paras.zh: 但白宫一位官员周五晚些时候在给CNBC的一份声明中表示：“该报道没有事实依据。”

paras.en: "Kevin Hassett is a key member of President Trump's economic team and will continue working to advance President Trump's economic policies," the official said on condition of anonymity to discuss the matter.
paras.zh: “凯文·哈塞特是特朗普总统经济团队的关键成员，将继续努力推进特朗普总统的经济政策。”这位官员在谈论此事时要求匿名。

paras.en: Zervos, reached by phone after Semafor's story published, declined to comment.
paras.zh: 在Semafor的报道发布后，Zervos通过电话联系，拒绝置评。

paras.zh: 这是突发新闻。请刷新以获取最新消息。

articles.title: Supreme Court agrees to hear Robinhood challenge to IPO information omission lawsuit

paras.en: The Supreme Court on Friday agreed to hear a case in which Robinhood seeks to block a class-action lawsuit over the omission of interim financial data from the online broker's initial public offering in 2021.
paras.zh: 美国最高法院周五同意审理一起案件，该案中Robinhood寻求阻止一项集体诉讼，该诉讼针对的是这家在线经纪商在2021年首次公开募股时未披露中期财务数据。

paras.en: Robinhood wants the Supreme Court to overturn a ruling by the 9th Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals that revived a lawsuit by investors against the company and firms involved with the IPO, including Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan Securities.
paras.zh: Robinhood希望最高法院推翻美国第九巡回上诉法院的一项裁决，该裁决恢复了投资者对该公司以及参与IPO的公司（包括高盛和摩根大通证券）的诉讼。

paras.en: A San Francisco federal court judge had previously dismissed the lawsuit.
paras.zh: 旧金山联邦法院的一名法官此前曾驳回该诉讼。

paras.en: The Trump administration and the Securities and Exchange Commission had urged the Supreme Court to hear Robinhood's appeal.
paras.zh: 特朗普政府和美国证券交易委员会曾敦促最高法院审理罗宾汉的上诉。

paras.en: "We are pleased the Supreme Court has agreed to hear our case and look forward to presenting our argument," a Robinhood spokesperson said in a statement.
paras.zh: “我们很高兴最高法院同意审理我们的案件，并期待着陈述我们的论点。”Robinhood的一位发言人在一份声明中表示。

paras.en: CNBC has requested comment from the attorneys representing the plaintiffs in the case.
paras.zh: CNBC已要求代表本案原告的律师发表评论。

paras.en: Robinhood's IPO came on the heels of a surge in investor interest during the Covid-19 pandemic of so-called meme stocks, and trading in the crypto asset Dogecoin.
paras.zh: 在新冠疫情期间，投资者对所谓的“梗股”以及加密资产狗狗币的交易兴趣激增，紧随其后，Robinhood就进行了IPO。

paras.en: In July 2021, Robinhood conducted its IPO, "for which it prepared a registration statement" that "contained only limited information about Robinhood's performance during the second quarter of 2021," the 9th Circuit panel that heard the case noted.
paras.zh: 第九巡回法庭审理该案的合议庭指出，2021年7月，Robinhood进行了IPO，“为此编制了一份注册声明”，该声明“仅包含有关Robinhood在2021年第二季度业绩的有限信息”。

paras.en: "After the initial public offering, Robinhood reported financial results from that second quarter, and its stock price dropped," the panel wrote.
paras.zh: “在首次公开募股之后，Robinhood公布了第二季度的财务业绩，其股价随即下跌。”该小组写道。

paras.en: The investors who sued Robinhood and the other defendants alleged that the registration statement omitted material information that was legally required to be disclosed.
paras.zh: 起诉罗宾汉和其他被告的投资者声称，招股说明书遗漏了法律要求披露的重要信息。

articles.title: CFTC Chair Selig tells CNBC crypto industry is embracing agency rules as legislation hopes fade

paras.en: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is already seeing demand from crypto exchanges planning to opt in to its newly proposed rules governing digital assets, according to Chairman Michael Selig.
paras.zh: 据主席迈克尔·塞利格（Michael Selig）透露，商品期货交易委员会（CFTC）已经看到加密货币交易所希望选择适用其新近提出的数字资产监管规则。

paras.en: The commodities regulator in October proposed rules aimed at preventing abuse in crypto markets and codifying crypto transaction rules under a federal rulebook. In the announcement, Selig said the move was a "critical step" in ensuring the United States remains the crypto capital of the world.
paras.zh: 10月，商品监管机构提出了旨在防止加密货币市场滥用的规则，并将加密货币交易规则纳入联邦法规。在公告中，塞利格表示，此举是确保美国保持世界加密货币之都地位的“关键一步”。

paras.en: Speaking this week at Cantor Convergence, an annual FinTech conference held in Miami Beach, Selig told CNBC in an exclusive interview that many of the major crypto exchanges are already registered with the CFTC because they offer financial derivatives, including perpetual futures, on their platforms and would now be able to add spot trading.
paras.zh: 本周在迈阿密海滩举行的年度金融科技会议Cantor Convergence上，塞利格在接受CNBC独家采访时表示，许多主要加密货币交易所已经向CFTC注册，因为它们在其平台上提供金融衍生品，包括永续期货，现在将能够增加现货交易。

paras.en: "We're also getting interest from new entrants who say, 'Look, signing up with 50 different state regimes is tough. We'd rather come to one regulator and get a license at the CFTC' so those new entrants are lining up to come register with us as well," he added.
paras.zh: “我们也吸引了一些新进入者的兴趣，他们说：‘你看，向50个不同的州政府部门注册很困难。我们宁愿找一个监管机构，在CFTC获得牌照，因此这些新进入者也在排队来我们这里注册。”他补充道。

paras.en: After the Clarity Act, a comprehensive market structure bill that established a regulatory framework for digital assets, stalled in the Senate in September, the CFTC and the SEC moved to establish federal frameworks using their existing statutory authorities.
paras.zh: 《Clarity法案》是一项全面的市场结构法案，旨在为数字资产建立监管框架，该法案于9月在参议院搁置。此后，CFTC和SEC着手利用其现有法定权力建立联邦框架。

paras.en: "We need to protect our markets and protect our customers using those markets so we'll continue to do exactly that in the wake of the Clarity Act failing to get the votes it needed to get to the president's desk during the current Congress," Selig said.
paras.zh: “我们需要保护我们的市场，并保护使用这些市场的客户，因此，在《Clarity法案》未能在本届国会期间获得所需票数以提交给总统的情况下，我们将继续这样做。”Selig表示。

paras.en: "Our statute does provide for authority of the agencies to register exchanges that want to offer margined, leveraged, or financed crypto assets or other types of commodity trading so we're utilizing that authority to allow our existing exchanges to begin offering these products under a regulated framework," he said.
paras.zh: 他说：“我们的法规确实规定了各机构有权对希望提供保证金、杠杆或融资加密资产或其他类型的商品交易的交易所进行注册，因此我们正在利用这一权力，允许我们现有的交易所在一个受监管的框架下开始提供这些产品。”

paras.en: Selig added that the oversight is opt-in for exchanges that are not currently offering margin leveraged financing, which is not permitted under existing state regimes.
paras.zh: Selig补充说，对于目前未提供保证金杠杆融资的交易所，监督是自愿性的，因为根据现行州级监管制度，此类融资是不被允许的。

paras.en: But the CFTC's new rules could face new scrutiny and oversight in 2027, with Democrats set to take control of the House and Senate after the midterms. Selig told CNBC he hopes the U.S. won't see a wave of software developers moving offshore, as many crypto businesses threatened to do under the Biden administration.
paras.zh: 不过，随着民主党在中期选举后将掌控众议院和参议院，CFTC的新规可能在2027年面临新的审查和监督。Selig在接受CNBC采访时表示，他希望美国不会出现大批软件开发人员迁往海外的情况，因为在拜登政府执政期间，许多加密货币企业都曾威胁要这样做。

paras.en: "I really hope that we learned lessons from the last several years in this space," he said.
paras.zh: “我真心希望，我们能从过去几年在这个领域所发生的事情中吸取教训。”他说。

paras.en: Crypto firms were at odds with Washington during the Biden administration, asking for clear operating rules, while also facing lawsuits brought by the SEC under former chair Gary Gensler's leadership. That shifted after President Donald Trump's 2024 victory.
paras.zh: 在拜登政府执政期间，加密货币公司与华盛顿存在分歧，要求制定明确的运营规则，同时还面临着美国证券交易委员会（SEC）在前主席加里·詹斯勒（Gary Gensler）领导下提起的诉讼。这种情况在唐纳德·特朗普总统于2024年赢得大选后发生了变化。

paras.en: "I do hope that we can work together with both sides of the aisle to protect software developers who want to do the right thing," Selig said, adding that those looking to commit crimes and engage in fraud should be held accountable.
paras.zh: “我真心希望我们能够与两党合作，保护那些想要做正确事情的软件开发者。”塞利格表示，并补充说，那些想要犯罪和从事欺诈行为的人应该承担责任。

paras.en: When asked whether he's prepared for increased scrutiny from Congress in 2027, Selig said, "Congress will do its job investigating where it needs to investigate."
paras.zh: 当被问及他是否已做好准备应对国会在2027年加强审查时，塞利格表示：“国会将履行职责，对需要调查的事项进行调查。”

paras.en: "I'm happy to answer any questions that Congress has for me just as I would answer Congress' questions today as I've done before hearing committees several times already," he said.
paras.zh: 他说：“我很乐意回答国会向我提出的任何问题，就像我今天会回答国会的问题一样，因为我已经多次在听证委员会上回答过问题。”

paras.en: Selig has also faced heat from Democrats for his handling of prediction markets. In February, 23 Democratic senators sent a letter to Chairman Selig urging him to reverse the agency's greenlighting of prediction markets.
paras.zh: 塞利格还因其对预测市场的处理方式而受到民主党的抨击。2月份，23名民主党参议员致函主席塞利格，敦促他撤销该机构对预测市场的批准。

paras.en: Selig has argued that prediction platforms are federally regulated as more states try to rein them in. The CFTC has sued several states to defend what the agency views as its exclusive jurisdiction to regulate event contracts, which it classifies as swaps.
paras.zh: 随着越来越多的州试图对预测平台进行监管，Selig 认为这些平台应受联邦监管。CFTC已对多个州提起诉讼，以捍卫该机构认为其对监管事件合约（该机构将其归类为掉期）的专属管辖权。

paras.en: "We're going to fight this up to the Supreme Court if that's where it's going," Selig said. "Our view on the statute is that we have exclusive jurisdiction over these markets, and I will not allow for states to go bring lawsuits against our exchanges, claiming that they're unlicensed gambling."
paras.zh: “如果事情发展到这一步，我们将一路抗争到最高法院。”塞利格表示。“我们对该法规的看法是，我们对这些市场拥有专属管辖权，我不会允许各州对我们的交易所提起诉讼，声称它们是非法赌博。”

paras.en: — CNBC's Tanaya Macheel contributed to this report.
paras.zh: — CNBC的Tanaya Macheel为本报道撰稿。

articles.title: No other animal walks like humans do. Here’s why

paras.en: Most humans walk without thinking too much of it. We put our foot down, heel first, and keep moving. But new work suggests this adaptation could be a uniquely human trade-off.
paras.zh: 大多数人走路时不会想太多。我们先放下脚后跟，然后继续前进。但一项新研究表明，这种适应性可能是人类独有的权衡取舍。

paras.en: A team of researchers captured high-speed, high-resolution videos of three chimps walking along a runway and analyzed existing walking data from 18 other chimps. When the animals walk on all fours, the team found, their foot position is variable—they might land heel first or touch down closer to their little toe. But when the chimps walk upright, they tend to favor midfoot strikes. In comparison, nine human study participants consistently walked heel first.
paras.zh: 一个研究团队拍摄了三只黑猩猩沿跑道行走的de高速、高分辨率视频，并分析了另外18只黑猩猩的现有行走数据。研究团队发现，当这些动物四肢着地行走时，它们的脚部着地位置并不固定——它们可能会先用脚跟着地，也可能用更靠近小脚趾的位置着地。但当黑猩猩直立行走时，它们倾向于用中足着地。相比之下，九名人r类研究参与者始终是先用脚跟着地。

paras.en: Other research on bonobos and orangutans suggests that those animals don’t consistently walk heel first. In fact, no other biped is known to walk that way, implying that “walking with a heel strike is a uniquely human thing,” says Pennsylvania State University and University of Buffalo anthropologist Nicholas Holowka, lead author of the study, published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA.
paras.zh: 其他关于倭黑猩猩和猩猩的研究表明，这些动物并不总是先用脚跟走路。事实上，据了解，没有其他双足动物会以这种方式行走，这意味着“以脚跟先着地的方式行走是人类独有的行为。”宾夕法尼亚州立大学和布法罗大学的人类学家尼古拉斯·霍洛卡（Nicholas Holowka）表示。他是该研究的第一作者，该研究发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The researchers then measured the impact forces on both humans’ and chimps’ feet and found a higher impact force with heel-first upright walking than with midfoot-first. But humans gained a measurable benefit from this movement strategy, too: walking midfoot first used 26 to 41 percent more energy than a heel-first gait.
paras.zh: 随后，研究人员测量了人类和黑猩猩双脚所受的冲击力，发现后脚跟先着地的直立行走方式所受的冲击力大于中足先着地的行走方式。但人类也从这种运动策略中获得了可衡量的益处：与先着地后跟的步态相比，先着地中足的步态消耗的能量多出26%至41%。

paras.en: Neelima Sharma, an evolutionary biologist at University College London who was not involved in the research, finds it interesting that human walking prioritizes energy savings, in contrast to running, during which humans typically avoid a heel-first stride “because your joints would be under much more impact force.” When we run, the peak load on the knee can be up to three times higher than it is while we’re walking.
paras.zh: 伦敦大学学院的进化生物学家Neelima Sharma没有参与这项研究，她认为，与跑步相比，人类行走时优先考虑节省能量，这一点很有意思。跑步时，人类通常会避免脚后跟先着地，“因为关节会承受更大的冲击力。” 跑步时，膝盖承受的峰值负荷可能比走路时高出三倍。

paras.en: By digging into the fossil record, the researchers tracked widening heel bones and growing lower-limb joints in bipedal human ancestors, beginning about three to four million years ago. By around two million years ago hominins consistently had wider heels and joints. Along with attributes such as longer legs and a modern pelvis, “the ability to heel strike safely is part of this suite of features that appears around two million years ago,” Holowka says. This time period also marks the emergence of hunting and gathering, with its long, energy-intensive journeys.
